label: copy-phase input q (fed-back output) at later recall positions
explanation: Reset-gate unit that fires mostly in the copy phase (94% of activation mass), concentrated on the last few copy steps (rate rises with t; to_go 0-1 holds about 78% of mass). The dominant driver is the fed-back input token q: q steps hold 67% of mass, with a lift of 17.7x, and every top activation is q being input during the copy phase. Weaker contributions come from x (12%), 3, v, l and d. It is nearly silent in the original phase (only t=2, about 5% of mass) and silent at the delimiter. Copy-phase q at recall_idx >= 4 reaches dev precision 0.66 but recall only 0.42 (mass 0.58). Restricting to recall_idx >= 5 raises precision to 0.77. The misses are diffuse: assorted tokens (x, 3, v, k) at late copy steps, plus q at short-L positions. Some q inputs at late steps stay inactive, so the token alone does not decide firing. Adding x clauses did not clearly help.
